rdfs:label: trustedApp
rdfs:comment: On a WebID profile, an app (by its acl:origin) the owner trusts, with the acl:mode values it may use. Legacy NSS mechanism: a request from that Origin succeeds only if the user is allowed by the resource's ACL AND the origin is listed with the mode — it narrows, never bypasses.
notes: An origin allow-list from the Node Solid Server (NSS) era: each `trustedApp` value carries `acl:origin` (the app's URL origin) and `acl:mode` (the modes the app may use). Both WAC and trustedApp must allow a request; it is never a pod-wide grant. Not defined in the W3C ACL ontology (an NSS convention only), not part of the WAC spec, and not supported by the Community Solid Server (CSS). The spec-defined way to restrict by app origin is `acl:origin` on an Authorization; Solid-OIDC client identifiers and ACP supersede it.

examples.title: Profile listing an app origin trusted for Read+Write
